六级大纲词汇 · 16英文原文

The Letter That Crossed Twice

两次穿过边境的信 · 595 词 · 6 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1After a military coup, a repressive regime closed an evening school near the border. It called the teachers dissidents and described their literacy classes as a pretext for spreading a hostile ideology. A bureaucratic order used curfew to suppress dissent. It curtailed travel and made open opposition futile. Irena, one of the teachers, kept a letter naming people who had learned to read. One was a juvenile whose father had disappeared in a crackdown. The school had become a target of ideological repression after he protested a rule on segregation. She decided to carry the letter to a consul who might be able to trace him.

2A courier offered to smuggle it across the river. His work had shifted from smuggling medicine during an embargo to carrying letters the regime wanted to stifle. Irena feared that being caught with an illicit document would lead to detention or deportation. She asked him to take a copy instead of the signed original. At a consulate on the other side, a clerk found that the father had applied for asylum. His application was pending because officials could not verify the name he used. The letter gave his old school name and a second address.

3Irena crossed openly on a permit once the consul invited her to testify. An officer at the checkpoint accused her of helping a smuggler. She answered with tact and let him inspect a copy. He threatened to deport her if she broke the terms of the permit. He did not see the signed page naming the boy. A bilateral arrangement protected sealed documents carried for a hearing. The permit would expire after a day. A multilateral agreement might end indefinite detention. It could not help at that day's hearing. She had to make that day's hearing count.

4At the hearing an official asked whether the father's claim rested on a political denunciation. Irena said he had opposed a tribal rule that segregated children of exiles from other pupils. He joined her class illiterate. He feared the same illiteracy for his son. A feminist lawyer helping the family explained how the closure had made the boy dependent on a single official for permission to study. Their immediate request was for a humane decision on the father's status. It did not require anyone to endorse his political views.

5A witness called him a militant who would kidnap a guard and hold him hostage. Irena produced another record showing that he had called on both sides to disarm during an earlier revolt. The call for disarmament did not settle every charge. It ran against the ruling bloc's account. It did help refute the claim that his classes were meant to prolong unrest. A reconciliatory statement from the village asked the authorities to let the family reunite. The official granted the asylum request and made clear which part of the testimony had established the man's identity.

6Irena returned with the letter and the decision. Officials had questioned the legitimacy of the father's claim. Now the same office had to record its own answer. The boy wanted to hear about the hearing. She let him read the part naming his father. Some classmates had been taught to assimilate by hiding their home language. That forced assimilation could deepen their alienation. He was afraid to say his father's old name aloud. She waited while he tried. It took him twice to get through the line. For Irena, literacy had always been a modest kind of emancipation. That night its meaning fit inside one sentence a child could read for himself.

六级大纲词汇 · 16中文译文

两次穿过边境的信

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1军事政变之后，当局关闭了边境附近的一所夜校，把老师称为持不同政见者，把识字课说成传播敌对思想的借口。行政命令以宵禁压制异议。出行受到限制，公开反对也难以奏效。老师伊琳娜保存着一封信，上面写着学会读书的人的名字。其中有个少年，父亲在一次镇压中失踪。他曾抗议一条实行隔离的规定，后来学校也成了思想压制的目标。伊琳娜决定把信交给可能找到他父亲的领事。

2一个信使主动提出帮她把信偷偷带过河。他过去在禁运期间运药，现在改为传递当局想扣下的信件。伊琳娜担心有人带着未经许可的文件被抓，会遭到拘留或驱逐。她请他带复印件过去，把有签名的原件留下。河对岸的领事馆里，一名职员查到孩子的父亲已经申请庇护。因为官员还无法核实他用的名字，申请一直待审。信上有他以前在学校用的名字，还有另一个地址。

3领事请伊琳娜去作证后，她拿着通行证公开过境。检查站的官员指责她帮助走私者。她得体地应答，把复印件给他看。官员警告，如果违反通行证规定，就要把她驱逐出去。他没有看到写着少年名字的签名页。双边安排保护为听证携带的密封文件。通行证只在当天有效。多边协议也许有一天能结束无限期拘留，但帮不上当天的听证。伊琳娜必须把握这一天。

4听证会上，一名官员问，父亲的申请是否基于一次政治告发。伊琳娜说，他反对过一条把流亡者子女和其他学生分开的部族规定。他来上识字班时还不认字，不想让儿子也落入同样的处境。一位帮助这个家庭的女权主义律师解释，学校关停以后，孩子能不能学习，全要一名官员批准。他们眼下需要的是对父亲身份作出合乎人情的决定，无须任何人认同他的政治立场。

5一名证人称父亲是个激进分子，会绑架看守，把他扣作人质。伊琳娜拿出另一份记录，显示在早些时候的暴动中，他曾呼吁双方解除武装。这份记录无法解释所有指控，却与执政集团的说法冲突，有助于驳斥他的识字课旨在延续动乱的指责。村里也提出和解声明，请当局准许父子团聚。官员同意了庇护申请，并说明是哪部分证词确认了父亲的身份。

6伊琳娜带着信和决定书回来。官员曾质疑父亲申请的正当性，如今同一个办事处得把自己的答复写进记录。孩子问起听证会。伊琳娜让他读写着父亲名字的那一段。有些同学被教着把家乡话藏起来，好融入当地。这种强迫同化反而让他们感到更加疏离。少年不敢念父亲原来的名字。她等他慢慢试。读了两遍，他终于把那一行念完。伊琳娜一直觉得，识字能给人一点自由。那天夜里，这份自由就放在一个孩子自己能读出的句子里。
